correctness.rationale: At each vertex the common outward cyclic edge-length order forces consecutive radial edge colors to advance by two modulo three. Hence the valence is divisible by three, and every three incident corners use the three angles of the fixed scalene triangle exactly once. The planar angle sum is \(d\pi/3\), strictly less than \(2\pi\) for a genuine convex vertex, so every valence is three. Euler forces a tetrahedron. Equal scalene face incidences make equal edges opposite; the standard explicit disphenoid coordinates exist precisely for acute triangles and have common outward chirality. The standalone integer-combinatorial verifier passed finite checks, but no infinite claim depends on it.

value.rationale: Provides a complete resolution, under the explicit outward-normal handedness convention, of the right/obtuse scalene realization question identified as still open by Georgiou 2026. The local curvature quantization is structural, bounds arbitrary face counts, and gives an exact tetrahedral classification, substantially beyond a routine recomputation of the known acute disphenoid case.
